rows.why: False for the first mold: は…より…です (電車はバスより速いです) has no のほうが; its winner is the は topic. The lead now says which marker carries the winner in each mold. Found by w08b_lesson_bodies.verdict.json found_not_in_scope[0].
rows.authored_to: Repare que, em todos, </text><jp>より</jp><text> continua colado no termo menor. O lado que ganha vem com </text><jp>は</jp><text> no primeiro e com </text><jp>のほうが</jp><text> nos outros dois; o que muda é só por onde a frase começa.
rows.verifier_problem: (3) Half-fixed. The new lead names two differences between the molds (the winner takes は in the first, のほうが in the other two) and then keeps the original tail 'o que muda é só por onde a frase começa', which the same sentence has just contradicted. It is also false on its own terms: は…より…です and のほうが…より both begin with the winning side (電車は／電車のほうが … バスより), so between them the start does NOT change; only the marker does. The 'only the start changes' claim holds for the last two molds only. Fix keeps both markers and scopes 'only the start' to those two. Measured: old_span count 1 in HEAD, in the post-merge body and after W08b rows 4-7 (both the input rows and the verdict-corrected row 6); LessonParser 0 errors before and after, with this correction too.

spans.from: o japonês </text><text weight="bold">não tem</text><text> uma palavra solta para "mais".
spans.to: a comparação </text><text weight="bold">não precisa</text><text> de uma palavra para "mais".

rows.why: Japanese does have a word for 'more' (もっと, N5); what is true is that the より comparative does not need one. Same correction w08b_merges.verdict.json made in yori-hou-ga#nuance. もっと is deliberately not named here, so no new vocab address enters the body. found_not_in_scope[1].
